recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. Revisit only if Pharmacy later changes the MedicationRequest.performer element or intentionally renames/removes the intended-performer search parameter.
issue_request: FHIR-13449 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy issue for STU3 requesting a search parameter for MedicationRequest.intendedPerformer after the intended performer element was added, so users could retrieve MedicationRequest resources by intended administration performer.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 333047669dbe6165ff81da07eabda57b3f9880e6 explicitly applied TR#13449 by adding an intended-performer reference search row with path MedicationRequest.performer to the MedicationRequest spreadsheet source. The companion intended performer element had been added by FHIR-12439 in commit 4b21106775caa782aa07057cdc51cb67b83f467f.
additional_context: The current build-source shape has been refactored from the old spreadsheet into source/medicationrequest/bundle-MedicationRequest-search-params.xml. The active MedicationRequest structure definition uses MedicationRequest.performer with short text 'Intended performer of administration', preserving the old intendedPerformer meaning. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting or more specific community guidance.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. The active MedicationRequest search-parameter bundle defines MedicationRequest-intended-performer with code intended-performer, type reference, and expression MedicationRequest.performer, and source/fhir.ini lists MedicationRequest as an active resource.
